items.followUp: Who discovered the role of ATP in energy transfer, and in what year did he receive the Nobel Prize?

rubric.why: Identifies the discoverer of ATP and the year of its discovery.
rubric.how: Award the mark for naming Karl Lohmann and giving 1929 as the discovery year.

rubric.why: Identifies the scientist associated with ATP’s role in energy transfer and his Nobel Prize year.
rubric.description: Fritz Lipmann received the Nobel Prize in 1953.
rubric.how: Award the mark for naming Fritz Lipmann and giving 1953.

modelAnswer: ATP was discovered by Karl Lohmann in 1929.
Fritz Lipmann, who explained the role of ATP in energy transfer, received the Nobel Prize in 1953.

items.followUp: How does light intensity affect the rate of photosynthesis?

rubric.why: States the effect of increasing carbon dioxide concentration on photosynthesis.
rubric.description: Increasing CO₂ concentration increases the rate of photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award the mark for stating that the rate rises as CO₂ concentration increases.

rubric.why: Explains what happens when CO₂ is no longer the limiting factor.
rubric.description: The rate eventually levels off when another factor becomes limiting.
rubric.how: Award the mark for noting that the rate reaches a plateau or stops increasing.

modelAnswer: As carbon dioxide concentration increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases, provided other factors are not limiting.
The rate eventually levels off when another factor becomes limiting.

rubric.why: Identifies that aerobic respiration requires oxygen.
rubric.description: Aerobic respiration is respiration that takes place in the presence of oxygen.
rubric.how: Award the mark for stating that oxygen is required or present.

rubric.why: Describes the complete breakdown of glucose and its products.
rubric.description: Glucose is completely broken down to carbon dioxide and water, releasing energy.
rubric.how: Award the mark for the complete breakdown/products and energy release.

modelAnswer: Aerobic respiration is the process in which glucose is completely broken down in the presence of oxygen.
It releases energy and produces carbon dioxide and water.

items.followUp: Name four foods that are good sources of proteins.

rubric.description: Names two animal sources of lipids.
rubric.how: Award the mark for any two correct animal sources, such as butter, ghee, milk, or egg yolk.

rubric.description: Names two plant sources of lipids.
rubric.how: Award the mark for any two correct plant sources, such as vegetable oils, nuts, or seeds.

modelAnswer: Four sources of lipids are butter, ghee, vegetable oils, and nuts.

items.followUp: Describe two functions of the stomach.

rubric.why: Identifies the mechanical digestion that occurs in the oral cavity.
rubric.description: The teeth chew and break food into smaller pieces.
rubric.how: Award the mark for mentioning chewing or mastication.

rubric.why: Identifies the beginning of chemical digestion in the mouth.
rubric.description: Saliva moistens food and begins the digestion of starch.
rubric.how: Award the mark for explaining that saliva begins starch digestion.

modelAnswer: The teeth in the oral cavity chew food into smaller pieces (mastication).
Saliva moistens food and begins the digestion of starch.

items.followUp: What is appendicitis? Name one symptom.

rubric.description: The appendix is a small, blind-ended, finger-like tube attached to the caecum.
rubric.how: Award the mark for identifying the appendix as a small projection attached to the caecum.

rubric.description: A symptom may be abdominal pain, often in the lower right abdomen; nausea or fever may also occur.
rubric.how: Award the mark for any one valid symptom.

modelAnswer: The appendix is a small, blind-ended, finger-like tube attached to the caecum.
A symptom of appendicitis is pain in the lower right part of the abdomen.

rubric.why: Defines a source by its role in supplying sugars.
rubric.description: A source is a plant part that produces or releases sugars for transport, such as a leaf.
rubric.how: Award the mark for stating that a source supplies sugars.

rubric.why: Defines a sink by its role in using or storing sugars.
rubric.description: A sink is a plant part that uses or stores transported sugars, such as a root or fruit.
rubric.how: Award the mark for stating that a sink uses or stores sugars.

modelAnswer: A source is a plant part, such as a leaf, that produces or releases sugars for transport.
A sink is a plant part, such as a root or fruit, that uses or stores transported sugars.

items.followUp: What distinguishes Rh-positive blood from Rh-negative blood?

rubric.why: Identifies the basis of the Rh blood group system.
rubric.description: The Rh system classifies blood according to the presence or absence of the Rh (D) antigen on red blood cells.
rubric.how: Award the mark for identifying the Rh antigen on red blood cells as the basis of the system.

rubric.why: Distinguishes the two Rh blood group categories.
rubric.description: Rh-positive blood has the antigen; Rh-negative blood lacks it.
rubric.how: Award the mark for correctly distinguishing Rh-positive from Rh-negative blood.

modelAnswer: The Rh blood group system classifies blood according to whether the Rh (D) antigen is present on red blood cells.
Rh-positive blood has this antigen, while Rh-negative blood lacks it.
